title: Royal Portuguese Cabinet of Reading, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
caption: Bookishly extravagant
subtitle: Royal Portuguese Cabinet of Reading, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
description:
Today we're inside the Royal Portuguese Cabinet of Reading in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, where the humble act of opening a book took on grand architectural ambitions. Founded in 1837 by 43 Portuguese immigrants, just 15 years after Brazil's independence, the institution eventually moved into the building seen here, completed half a century later in a lavish Neo-Manueline style. Shelves soar over 20 metres around a vast reading room, crowned by a monumental stained-glass skylight that makes daylight part of the design.
The building became a bridge between two countries: its façade was carved in Lisbon, shipped across the Atlantic and assembled in Rio. So striking was the result that it was ranked among the 20 most beautiful libraries in the world in 2014. Opened to the public in 1900, it now preserves hundreds of thousands of volumes, making it the largest collection of Portuguese literature outside Portugal. Yet beneath all that ornate grandeur, the original idea remains wonderfully simple: give people access to books.

title: Mount Sneffels in the San Juan Mountains near Ridgway, Colorado, United States
caption: 'Peak' into Colorado
subtitle: Mount Sneffels in the San Juan Mountains near Ridgway, Colorado
description:
Some mountains make you work for the view. Mount Sneffels makes you work for the last few hundred metres. Rising to 4,310 metres in Colorado's San Juan Mountains, this fourteener is a familiar sight around Ridgway, Ouray and Telluride. It sits within the 67-square-kilometre Mount Sneffels Wilderness, a protected area designated in 1980. Hikers can reach the mountain from several approaches, including the Yankee Boy Basin and the Blue Lakes area.
The mountain itself is geologically distinctive: unlike many of its nearby peaks, Mount Sneffels is largely made of an intrusion of igneous rock that pushed into older volcanic deposits. Below its western flank, Blue Lakes fill a deep alpine basin and offer another way to experience the area. The peak also rises above the tree line, where the landscape becomes noticeably more exposed and rocky. Keep an eye on the sky because mountain weather loves a plot twist. Check the forecast and start early, and bring layers, water and the right gear for the conditions.

title: Autumn waterfalls near Sitovo, Plovdiv Province, Bulgaria
caption: Nature's fall soundtrack
subtitle: Autumn waterfalls near Sitovo, Plovdiv Province, Bulgaria
description:
In Bulgaria's Western Rhodope Mountains, autumn leaves gather beside the rushing waters of Sitovo Waterfall. Near the village of Sitovo, southwest of Plovdiv, the falls tumble beneath an old stone bridge whose arch frames the cascades like a storybook scene. Moss-covered stones and pine trees add shades of green to the autumn landscape, while fallen leaves gather along the water's edge or drift through its pools. The falls become especially lively after rain and during spring snowmelt, when the surrounding woodland echoes with the sound of rushing water.
Sitovo offers more than natural scenery. The village preserves traditional Rhodope homes, while nearby rock shelters are home to the mysterious Sitovo Inscription, a series of symbols carved into stone. First documented in 1928, the inscription remains undeciphered, with its origin, language, meaning and date still uncertain. Here, water, stone, forest and mystery meet in one of Bulgaria's quieter corners.

title: A grove of pond cypress trees with fall foliage, Georgia, United States
caption: Nature's golden mirror
subtitle: A grove of pond cypress trees with fall foliage, Georgia, USA
description:
Reflected in calm water and glowing in the light of the setting sun, this grove of pond cypress creates a striking display of colour and symmetry. Native to the southeastern United States, the species is associated with shallow ponds, depressions and wetland habitats. This image was captured in Georgia, where these trees can be found in places such as the Okefenokee Swamp and other low-lying wetlands.
Unlike most conifers, pond cypress sheds its needle-like foliage each fall, taking on warm yellow, copper and orange-brown tones. Closely related to the more widespread bald cypress, it is generally smaller and more strongly associated with still or shallow water.
Cypress wetlands provide important habitat and nesting sites for birds, amphibians and other wildlife. Here, glowing reflections, dark trunks and sunlight transform the wetland into a nearly painterly landscape, revealing the quiet beauty of the American South.

title: Kunětická hora Castle, Bohemia, Czechia
caption: Where history stands watch
subtitle: Kunětická hora Castle, Bohemia, Czechia
description:
What stories could these walls tell? Rising above eastern Bohemia in Czechia, Kunětická hora Castle has witnessed centuries of history. Dating to the late 14th century, the castle gradually evolved into an impressive fortress and noble residence. Its elevated position offered commanding views of the surrounding countryside and helped make it an important stronghold.
The complex reached its height in the 16th century, when the powerful Pernštejn family transformed it into a grand late Gothic and Renaissance stronghold. Later centuries brought decline and neglect, and parts of the site were even lost to stone quarrying. Restoration began in the early 20th century, helping preserve the landmark visitors see today.
Visitors can explore historic rooms and exhibitions, climb the tower for panoramic views and discover the legends associated with the castle. Rising above the Elbe lowlands, Kunětická hora Castle remains a striking reminder of Bohemia's medieval past.

title: Standing stones at Avebury in Wiltshire, England
caption: Where mist meets millennia
subtitle: Standing stones at Avebury in Wiltshire, England
description:
As morning mist drifts among the standing stones of Avebury in Wiltshire, England, the scene feels almost timeless. These ancient megaliths form part of one of the world's most remarkable prehistoric landscapes, centred on a vast Neolithic monument built around 4,500 years ago. Avebury contains the world's largest prehistoric stone circle, as well as a massive henge and stone avenues extending into the surrounding countryside. Together with nearby monuments such as Silbury Hill and West Kennet Avenue, it forms part of an extensive Neolithic complex that has fascinated generations of visitors, researchers and archaeologists.
Unlike many archaeological sites, Avebury allows visitors to walk among the stones themselves. Designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site as part of the Stonehenge, Avebury and Associated Sites World Heritage property, it offers a rare opportunity to experience a prehistoric setting where ancient monuments remain integrated with the modern countryside. While the precise purposes and meanings of these monuments remain uncertain, their scale is unmistakable.

title: Sandhill cranes, Bosque del Apache National Wildlife Refuge, New Mexico, USA
caption: Time to fly high
subtitle: Sandhill cranes, New Mexico, USA
description: Winter transforms Bosque del Apache National Wildlife Refuge in New Mexico into a haven for wildlife. Established in 1939, the 57,331-acre sanctuary provides an important stopover for migrating waterfowl and supports wildlife year-round. Sandhill cranes, featured in today's image, arrive in late October and spend the winter here, roosting in shallow water at night and feeding in nearby fields at sunrise. The refuge is a key wintering ground for the Rocky Mountain population of sandhill cranes. Other seasonal visitors include snow geese, northern pintails, hawks and eagles, while mule deer, coyotes and other mammals inhabit its diverse habitats.

title: St. Bartholomew's Cathedral in Frankfurt, Germany
caption: Ghosts of empires past
description: Frankfurt, Germany, provides a fitting backdrop for Halloween with St. Bartholomew's Cathedral and its striking Gothic tower. Yet the holiday's origins are even more intriguing. Many Halloween traditions are linked to Samhain, an ancient Celtic festival marking the end of the harvest season and the start of winter. People believed the boundary between the living and the dead grew thin, prompting bonfires, offerings and disguises to ward off wandering spirits. Later, the Christian observances of All Saints' Day and All Souls' Day helped shape Halloween as we know it today. St. Bartholomew's may set the scene, but Halloween brings the ghosts, legends and mystery.
